official.deadline_note: MEXT publishes no central deadline: 'The deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission. Make sure to confirm the deadline at the website of the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of your nationality or in some other way.' Published MEXT timeline for the 2027 cycle: call for applications opens around mid-April 2026; First Screening around early May to late July 2026; request for provisional acceptance until September 1, 2026; Placement Preference Application Form mid-September to early October 2026; Second Screening and university placement from November 2026; results notified from January to March 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cycle - arrival April 2027 (April term: in principle arrive between April 1 and 7, 2027) or October 2027; applications open around mid-April 2026, results January-March 2027
official.status_note: MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under 'programmes currently being recruited' (募集中のプログラム) on its Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship system page, which also states that all procedures are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your country, or institutions of higher education in Japan. MEXT publishes no central opening or closing date; each Japanese diplomatic mission sets and publishes its own deadlines and screening dates, and the type and field of application may vary from country to country.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Education fees: 'Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered.' The entrance examination fee, however, will be borne by the grantees if they cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university.
benefits: Allowance: 143,000 yen per month for students receiving the preparatory education and non-regular students; 144,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in master's or professional degree courses; 145,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in doctoral courses
A supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month will be added for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered

Transportation to Japan: MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route, and provides an economy-class airline ticket from the international airport nearest the grantee's residence to an international airport in Japan

Transportation from Japan: based on the application by the grantee, MEXT will provide an economy-class airline ticket to grantees who will graduate from the accepting university and return to the home country by the end of the final month of the period of scholarship
The first 6-month period of the scholarship will be devoted to preparatory education in the Japanese language for those who require such education
eligibility: Nationality: applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; an applicant who has Japanese nationality at the time of application is not eligible (dual nationality exception applies)
Age: applicants, in principle, must have been born on or after April 2, 1992

Academic background: 16 years of school education, a 3+ year programme with a bachelor's-equivalent degree, or other admission eligibility for a master's/doctoral (first phase) course; an overseas degree equivalent to a master's degree for a doctoral course (second phase); 18 years of school education for doctoral courses in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and certain pharmaceutical fields
Japanese language: applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, and must have the ability to conduct research and adapt to living in Japan
Health: applicants must submit a health certificate in the prescribed format signed by a physician attesting that the applicant has no physical or mental conditions hindering study in Japan

Arrival in Japan: applicants must choose either the April term (in principle arrive between April 1 and 7, 2027) or the October term; in principle, a change in the arrival period is not permitted after submission of the Application Form
requirements: Application must be made through the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of the applicant's nationality; the deadline and screening dates are set by each mission, not by MEXT centrally

First Screening at the mission consists of examination of submitted application documents, written examinations of language proficiency in Japanese and English (both must be taken by all applicants; the English proficiency test may be exempted for countries where English is the official language), and an interview
All submitted documents must be written in Japanese or English, or if written in any other language, accompanied by a translation in Japanese or English

Applicants shall, in principle, newly obtain a 'Student' visa at the Japanese diplomatic mission in their country/region of nationality before travelling to Japan; scholarship payment is suspended if the applicant comes to Japan without it
The application is free of charge; MEXT warns that organisations or individuals charging application fees or deposits have no relation with the Japanese Government
documents: ① Application Form, ② Placement Preference Application Form, and ③ Field of Study and Research Plan - use the 2027 forms (① and ③ original plus 2 copies; ② original)

④ Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended (must show the grade scale applied and grades earned in all subjects each year; a degree certificate or ranking certificate will not substitute) and ⑤ Certification of graduation or degree certificate (or certificate of prospective graduation if not yet graduated) - original plus 2 copies

⑥ Recommendation letter from the president/dean or the academic advisor at the current or last university attended (free format) and ⑦ Medical certificate in the prescribed format - original plus 2 copies

Conditional items: ⑧ Abstracts of theses (if the applicant has written theses), ⑨ Certificate of language proficiency in Japanese or English (only if held; 3 copies; issued no earlier than two years before the date of application), ⑩ Recommendation letter from the present employer (if currently employed), ⑪ Photographs of the applicant's own works of art or digitally recorded media of musical performance (if majoring in fine arts or music)

Applicant photograph: 4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper-body, full-faced, no hats, taken within six months of submission, printed on paper specially for photographs, with the applicant's name and nationality written on the back

Write the document number (① to ⑪) in the upper right-hand corner of the first page of all documents; documents in bound form may be dismantled during the review process, and submitted documents will not be returned
selection_criteria: Examination of submitted application documents: must show that the applicant's academic achievement at the university last graduated from equaled or exceeded a certain level, and state the research plan in a detailed and concrete manner
Written examination of language proficiency: must show language proficiency adequate for research in a Japanese university

Interview: must reveal a clear sense of purpose relating to study in Japan, that the applicant has gathered information about Japanese universities, and sufficient Japanese or English language ability to communicate with an academic advisor in Japan

A letter of provisional acceptance greatly influences final selection results; applicants may be rejected if they have not obtained any such letter, and applications without any acceptance are rejected at placement

MEXT conducts the Second Screening based on the First Screening results; an application may be rejected if it arouses weapons proliferation concerns, including those over weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and related items
coverage: Tuition, entrance examination and matriculation fees waivered (education fees exemption)
Monthly scholarship of 143,000-145,000 yen depending on the course enrolled (preparatory education/non-regular 143,000; regular master's/professional 144,000; doctoral 145,000)
Supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 or 3,000 yen per month in specially designated regions
Round-trip economy-class airfare to and from Japan on MEXT-stipulated routes
Japanese-language preparatory education for up to the first 6 months where the accepting university or MEXT deems it necessary
application_method: Confirm with the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country whether the Research Student type and the field you wish to apply for are open, and obtain its deadline and screening dates
Submit the full document set to the mission by its deadline; sit the document examination, the Japanese and English written examinations, and the interview (First Screening)

Applicants who pass the First Screening directly contact the Japanese universities they wish to enter to request letters of provisional acceptance (from September 1, 2026; up to two universities at a time, maximum two letters in total)
Submit the completed Placement Preference Application Form based on the universities' responses to the Japanese diplomatic mission by its deadline (mid-September to early October 2026)
MEXT conducts the Second Screening and university placement (from November 2026); final selection results and the accepting university are notified via the mission from January to March 2027
Travel to Japan with the MEXT-arranged economy-class airline ticket within the specified arrival period (April 1-7, 2027 for the April term)
official.application_route: Apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality (Embassy Recommendation route) - there is no central MEXT application portal; the mission collects documents, runs the first screening and forwards recommendations to MEXT
official.study_mode: Graduate-school research student, either regular or non-regular; the scholarship will be suspended for any period of extended absence from the university
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. Applicants with Japanese nationality are not eligible; dual nationals who hold Japanese nationality, reside outside Japan at the time of application, choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality by the date of arrival may apply, and the First Screening must be conducted at the mission of the chosen country.
official.international_eligibility: Designed for international students applying from outside Japan through the diplomatic mission of the country of their nationality. Ineligible: those already enrolled, or planning to enrol, in a Japanese university or other institution as a privately-financed international student from the time of application until the start of the scholarship payment period.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants should apply for the field of study they majored in at university or its related field(s), which must be subjects they will be able to study and research in graduate courses at Japanese universities. Fields may be restricted to particular fields specified by the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country. Traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki and classical Japanese dances, or subjects that require practical training in specific technologies at factories or companies, are not included. Medicine, dentistry and welfare science students cannot engage in clinical training until obtaining the relevant licence from the Minister of Health, Labor and Welfare.
official.research_requirement: The Field of Study and Research Plan (on the prescribed 2027 form) must describe the applicant's past and present field of study and research theme and plan in Japan; it serves as an important reference for university placement, and the research plan must be stated in a detailed and concrete manner to pass the document examination.
official.duration: Non-regular students: April 2027 until the end of March 2029 (April term) or September/October 2027 until the end of March 2029 (October term), with the first 6 months devoted to preparatory education in Japanese for those who require it. Regular students: the necessary period to complete the respective regular course (master's course standard period two years; doctoral course three years, or four years in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and 6-year-based pharmacy).
official.description: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) of Japan offers scholarships to international students who wish to study in graduate courses at Japanese universities as Research Students (either regular students or non-regular students) under the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship Program. Research Students are enrolled in a master's course, a doctoral course, or a professional graduate course, or conduct research in a specialized field with the aim of completing the course. For the 2027 Embassy Recommendation route, applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese diplomatic mission in their country, then placed by MEXT at a Japanese graduate school.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship, Embassy Recommendation (Research Students)
official.english_requirement: A written examination in English is part of the First Screening and must be taken by all applicants (the English proficiency test may be exempted for countries where English is the official language, per the mission's guidance). No minimum IELTS/TOEFL score is published; a certificate of Japanese or English language proficiency is submitted only if the applicant holds one (3 copies, issued no earlier than two years before the date of application).

not_confirmed: central deadline date - none is published; deadlines are set by each Japanese diplomatic mission
minimum English test score (IELTS/TOEFL) - none is published; English ability is assessed by the mission's written examination and interview
country-specific openings for the Research Student type and eligible fields - the type and field of application vary by country and are confirmed only by the applicant's own mission
whether an individual mission's 2027 submission window is still open at the time of reading
verification.notes: Amounts (143,000/144,000/145,000 yen per month, 2,000/3,000 yen regional allowance), fee waivers, travel provision, duration, application documents and process were read directly from MEXT's official 2027 Research Students English Application Guidelines PDF and the MEXT recruitment page; scholarship band and tuition/travel coverage cross-checked on the JASSO Study in Japan official page; no central deadline exists on any official page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fully funded MEXT research-student award for 2027 arrival - tuition waived, a 143,000-145,000 yen monthly stipend and round-trip airfare - but you apply through a Japanese embassy, not MEXT, and that embassy runs the first screening. Passing the first screening is only halfway: you must personally contact Japanese graduate schools from September 1, 2026 to obtain letters of provisional acceptance (maximum two universities at a time, maximum two letters in total), because MEXT rejects applicants who reach final selection without one. Check with your mission immediately about whether its 2027 submission window is still open, since MEXT publishes no central deadline, screening dates vary by country, and the published timeline put first screening roughly between May and July 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor's or master's graduates under 35 from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who can already name specific Japanese graduate schools and potential supervisors and are willing to learn Japanese.
application_readiness_checklist: Email or call the Japanese embassy/consulate in your country now to confirm the Research Student track, eligible fields, exact deadline and examination dates for the 2027 cycle

Complete the Field of Study and Research Plan on the official 2027 form early - it doubles as the placement document, so make the research theme concrete and name how it fits Japanese graduate schools

Order transcripts showing the grade scale and every subject each year, graduation or prospective-graduation certificates, and a dean/advisor recommendation letter well ahead of the mission deadline; originals go to the mission and are not returned
Complete the medical certificate on the prescribed form, and verify passport validity, nationality eligibility and the born-on-or-after-April-2-1992 age rule before applying
After passing the first screening, request the mission-stamped copies and email up to two universities at once; allow roughly one month per university to issue the provisional acceptance letter
Reserve funds for the first one to one-and-a-half months in Japan before the first stipend payment; MEXT recommends bringing approximately US$2,000
common_rejection_risks: No letter of provisional acceptance - MEXT states applicants may be rejected without one, and rejects the application at placement if no acceptance has been obtained
Contacting universities before September 1, 2026, contacting more than two universities simultaneously, or obtaining more than two acceptance letters
After a rejection, requesting an acceptance letter from another faculty member or graduate school at the same university, or lodging an objection to the university
Missing the embassy's own deadline or examination date - MEXT publishes none centrally and does not disclose screening reasons or dates beyond each mission's own notice
Arriving outside the stipulated April 1-7, 2027 window (or the university-specified October window) - travel expenses are not paid and the applicant must withdraw from the program

Automatic ineligibility: previous MEXT scholarship grantee (outside the 3+ year exceptions), failure to relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival, planning to receive another Japanese-government scholarship, or enrolment as a privately-financed student in Japan between application and the payment start
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel from home to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, carry-on and unaccompanied baggage expenses, accommodation and dormitory fees at the university (borne by the grantee), the entrance examination fee if you do not proceed to a master's/doctoral course or are not admitted, third-country travel and lodging if there is no direct flight or no Japanese mission in your country, and the first one to one-and-a-half months of living costs before the first payment (MEXT recommends bringing approximately US$2,000).
document_audit: Photograph: 4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper body, full face, no hat, taken within six months of submission, name and nationality written on the back
Transcripts must show the grade scale and grades for every subject studied each year; a degree certificate or a class-ranking certificate does not substitute
Everything must be in Japanese or English or carry a translation, and each document must carry its number ①-⑪ in the top right corner of the first page
Language certificates only count if issued within two years of the application date and are optional supplements - a missing certificate does not disqualify you, but a wrong-form or expired one can
Do not send irreplaceable originals - submitted documents are not returned and bound documents may be dismantled for review

Keep the mission-stamped copies of documents ① and ③-⑪; you must resend that stamped set to universities when requesting provisional acceptance, and a university cannot comply without the stamped First Screening passing certificate
alerts: There is no central deadline: if your embassy has already closed its 2027 submission window (MEXT's timeline put First Screening roughly May-July 2026), you are effectively locked out of this cycle - confirm with the mission before investing effort
University contact is only permitted after you pass the First Screening and from September 1, 2026; earlier approaches are not allowed, and contact made on September 2 or after is not permitted

Universities typically need about one month to issue a provisional acceptance letter, which is not their deadline - do not pressure them, but plan backwards from your mission's placement-form deadline
Placement partially ignores your preference order: where your list mixes private and national universities, the national university option is prioritised regardless of your ranking
Choose your arrival term carefully - the arrival period cannot be changed in principle after placement, even if your application form declared flexibility
Stipend payments go only to a Japan Post Bank account opened after arrival, and National Health Insurance enrolment is mandatory - plan your first month around that setup gap
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Embassy-level document submission and First Screening (roughly May-July 2026) -> direct emails to Japanese graduate schools for provisional acceptance (from September 1, 2026) -> Placement Preference Application Form to the embassy (mid-Sep to early Oct 2026) -> MEXT Second Screening and placement (from Nov 2026) -> results and accepting university notified via the embassy (Jan-Mar 2027) -> arrival in Japan April or October 2027.
